words.sense: Complete openness about a difficult truth, without requiring an abrasive manner.
misconceptions: Any unwelcome truth is automatically bluntness.

words.sense: A way of speaking so abruptly or sharply that it risks hurting feelings.
misconceptions: Polite language means someone cannot be candid.

semantic_axes.description: Candor is openness about the truth; bluntness draws attention to a sharp or insensitive way of delivering it.

edges.boundary_rule: Candor is openness about the truth; bluntness draws attention to a sharp or insensitive way of delivering it.

misconceptions.M1: Any unwelcome truth is automatically bluntness.
misconceptions.M2: Polite language means someone cannot be candid.
misconceptions.M3: A truthful insult is best judged only by its factual content.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Aisha’s response about the missing funds?

beats.text: Aisha told the group exactly how much money was missing and admitted she had forgotten to record two payments.
beats.decisive_clue: disclosed uncomfortable facts and her own omission
beats.reason: She openly supplies facts that could embarrass her.

beats.text: She made the explanation at a crowded meeting, though she could have sent it privately.
beats.decisive_clue: disclosed uncomfortable facts and her own omission; a larger audience changes nothing
beats.reason: The audience does not show that her words were cutting.

chains.feedback_short: Aisha disclosed the gap and her own mistake; speaking before a crowd did not make her wording abrasive.
chains.feedback_deep: Candor concerns openness, particularly when the facts are uncomfortable. Bluntness concerns the sharpness of expression. A public admission can be candid without being cruel.
chains.contrast_rule: Candor reveals the truth; bluntness can make the truth sting.

hints.attention: Notice what she reveals, not how many people listen.
hints.axis: Candor is openness about the truth; bluntness draws attention to a sharp or insensitive way of delivering it.
hints.contrast: Candor reveals the truth; bluntness can make the truth sting.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Mateo’s feedback to his singing partner?

beats.text: Mateo said the high notes were slipping and offered to practice the difficult section together.
beats.reason: He is open about a weakness while remaining considerate.

beats.text: His exact opening was, “Your voice ruins the song; everyone can hear it.”
beats.decisive_clue: the actual wording attacks the person
beats.reason: The revealed phrasing makes the sharp delivery more defining than his initial constructive summary.

chains.feedback_short: The exact words turned useful criticism into a cutting personal judgment.
chains.feedback_deep: Candor requires truthfulness and openness, not rudeness. Bluntness is marked by unsoftened, potentially insensitive phrasing; the quoted attack makes that the stronger label.
chains.contrast_rule: Candor reveals the truth; bluntness can make the truth sting.

hints.attention: Pay attention to the words he actually chose.
hints.axis: Candor is openness about the truth; bluntness draws attention to a sharp or insensitive way of delivering it.
hints.contrast: Candor reveals the truth; bluntness can make the truth sting.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Priya’s explanation to her brother?

beats.text: Priya explained that their planned holiday would cost more than they could afford, using the actual household bills.
beats.decisive_clue: used household bills to disclose an unwelcome affordability limit
beats.reason: She gave a clear financial assessment instead of letting her brother believe otherwise.

beats.text: She also explained which charges were estimates and which amounts came directly from receipts.
beats.decisive_clue: separated estimates from receipts when discussing affordability
beats.reason: The added precision strengthens her openness.

chains.feedback_short: Priya makes an unwelcome budget limit clear and distinguishes estimates from confirmed figures.
chains.feedback_deep: Candor is openness about difficult facts, including unpopular financial limits. Distinguishing estimates from receipts makes Priya’s explanation more transparent without introducing harsh language.
chains.contrast_rule: Candor reveals the truth; bluntness can make the truth sting.

hints.attention: Watch which facts she is willing to disclose.
hints.axis: Candor is openness about the truth; bluntness draws attention to a sharp or insensitive way of delivering it.
hints.contrast: Candor reveals the truth; bluntness can make the truth sting.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Jin’s comment on a friend’s product listing?

beats.text: Jin typed, “This looks cheap, and your photos make it worse.”
beats.decisive_clue: dismissive wording about the friend’s work
beats.reason: The assessment is delivered in a needlessly sharp manner.

beats.text: Jin later inspected the photos closely and found that the lighting really was poor.
beats.decisive_clue: dismissive wording remains despite factual support
beats.reason: Accuracy does not undo the abrasive way Jin spoke.

chains.feedback_short: Even if the photos needed work, “looks cheap” remained needlessly cutting.
chains.feedback_deep: Truthfulness can coexist with bluntness. The question here is how Jin spoke: his dismissive phrasing risks offense regardless of whether the criticism is accurate.
chains.contrast_rule: Candor reveals the truth; bluntness can make the truth sting.

hints.attention: Separate accuracy from the manner of delivery.
hints.axis: Candor is openness about the truth; bluntness draws attention to a sharp or insensitive way of delivering it.
hints.contrast: Candor reveals the truth; bluntness can make the truth sting.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Noura’s comments after the match?

beats.text: Noura told her teammate, “You were useless out there.”
beats.reason: Her words target the person rather than explaining a problem.

beats.text: She later explained that she was worried about the next match and wanted the teammate to improve.
beats.decisive_clue: the original put-down remains despite helpful intentions
beats.reason: A well-meant purpose does not soften what she actually said.

chains.feedback_short: Her desire to help does not erase the sting of “useless.”
chains.feedback_deep: Bluntness describes the delivery, not necessarily a malicious motive. A speaker can intend to help while using words that sound dismissive or hurtful.
chains.contrast_rule: Candor reveals the truth; bluntness can make the truth sting.

hints.attention: Judge the wording separately from the speaker’s goal.
hints.axis: Candor is openness about the truth; bluntness draws attention to a sharp or insensitive way of delivering it.
hints.contrast: Candor reveals the truth; bluntness can make the truth sting.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Leo’s reply to his manager?

beats.text: Leo told his manager, “I cannot say whether this will work; I have not tested it yet.”
beats.decisive_clue: admitted uncertainty instead of claiming confidence
beats.reason: He openly identifies what he does not yet know.

beats.text: He spoke briefly because his manager had another meeting in five minutes.
beats.reason: A short conversation does not make his words cutting.

chains.feedback_short: Leo acknowledges uncertainty rather than pretending to know; speaking briefly does not make his wording abrasive.
chains.feedback_deep: Candor is direct openness, especially about uncomfortable facts. Bluntness describes a sharp, insensitive manner. Brevity alone does not make a statement rude.
chains.contrast_rule: Candor reveals the truth; bluntness can make the truth sting.

hints.attention: Look at what Leo owns up to, not the length of his reply.
hints.axis: Candor is openness about the truth; bluntness draws attention to a sharp or insensitive way of delivering it.
hints.contrast: Candor reveals the truth; bluntness can make the truth sting.
